review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

24:1.sourceText: Μετὰ δὲ πέντε ἡμέρας κατέβη ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς Ἀνανίας μετὰ πρεσβυτέρων τινῶν καὶ ῥήτορος Τερτύλλου τινός, οἵτινες ἐνεφάνισαν τῷ ἡγεμόνι κατὰ τοῦ Παύλου.
24:1.targetText: Five days later the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and a lawyer named Tertullus, who presented to the governor their case against Paul.

groups.note: Μετά ("after") is rendered later.
ῥήτορος ("orator, advocate") is rendered lawyer.
τινός ("a certain") is rendered a.
ἐνεφάνισαν ("they brought charges") is rendered presented.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English introduces the name; the Greek has no word for "name" here.
English supplies the object of presented; the Greek verb has none.

24:2.sourceText: κληθέντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἤρξατο κατηγορεῖν ὁ Τέρτυλλος λέγων Πολλῆς εἰρήνης τυγχάνοντες διὰ σοῦ καὶ διορθωμάτων γινομένων τῷ ἔθνει τούτῳ διὰ τῆς σῆς προνοίας,
24:2.targetText: When Paul had been called in, Tertullus opened the prosecution: “Because of you, we have enjoyed a lasting peace, and your foresight has brought improvements to this nation.

groups.note: The genitive absolute κληθέντος ("having been called") is rendered as a when-clause.
The pronoun αὐτοῦ ("he") is rendered by the name Paul.
κατηγορεῖν ("to accuse") is rendered the prosecution.
Πολλῆς ("much") is rendered lasting.
BSB makes your foresight the subject; γινομένων ("coming about") is rendered has brought.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The participle λέγων ("saying") is represented only by the colon before the quotation.
BSB makes your foresight the subject, so διά ("through") has no English word.

24:3.sourceText: πάντῃ τε καὶ πανταχοῦ ἀποδεχόμεθα, κράτιστε Φῆλιξ, μετὰ πάσης εὐχαριστίας.
24:3.targetText: In every way and everywhere, most excellent Felix, we acknowledge this with all gratitude.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders τε … καί as a plain and, so τε has no separate English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of acknowledge.

24:4.sourceText: ἵνα δὲ μὴ ἐπὶ πλεῖόν σε ἐνκόπτω, παρακαλῶ ἀκοῦσαί σε ἡμῶν συντόμως τῇ σῇ ἐπιεικείᾳ.
24:4.targetText: But in order not to burden you any further, I beg your indulgence to hear us briefly.

groups.note: ἐπὶ πλεῖον ("for more") is rendered any further.
ἐνκόπτω ("I hinder, weary") is rendered to burden.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB recasts "I beg you to hear" as I beg your indulgence to hear, so this second σε ("you"), the subject of ἀκοῦσαι, has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

24:5.sourceText: εὑρόντες γὰρ τὸν ἄνδρα τοῦτον λοιμὸν καὶ κινοῦντα στάσεις πᾶσιν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις τοῖς κατὰ τὴν οἰκουμένην πρωτοστάτην τε τῆς τῶν Ναζωραίων αἱρέσεως,
24:5.targetText: We have found this man to be a pestilence, stirring up dissension among the Jews all over the world. He is a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes,

groups.note: πᾶσιν ("all") is rendered by the all of all over.
κατά ("throughout") is rendered over; with πᾶσιν it gives all over.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB sets stirring up beside pestilence without and, so καί has no English word.
BSB starts a new sentence here, so τε ("and") has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies to be; the Greek sets the noun beside the object.
English supplies a subject and verb for the new sentence.

24:6.sourceText: ὃς καὶ τὸ ἱερὸν ἐπείρασεν βεβηλῶσαι, ὃν καὶ ἐκρατήσαμεν,
24:6.targetText: and he even tried to desecrate the temple; so we seized him.

groups.note: The relative ὅς ("who") is rendered and he, as BSB continues the sentence.
The relative ὅν ("whom") is rendered him.
The καί before ἐκρατήσαμεν is rendered so.

24:8.sourceText: παρ’ οὗ δυνήσῃ αὐτὸς ἀνακρίνας περὶ πάντων τούτων ἐπιγνῶναι ὧν ἡμεῖς κατηγοροῦμεν αὐτοῦ.
24:8.targetText: By examining him yourself, you will be able to learn the truth about all our charges against him.”

groups.note: The relative οὗ ("whom") is rendered him, the one examined.
κατηγοροῦμεν ("we accuse") is rendered our charges.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB makes the relative the object of examining, so παρά ("from") has no English word.
BSB leaves τούτων ("these") unexpressed; all our charges stands for the whole phrase.
BSB folds the relative ὧν ("of which") into the noun phrase our charges.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of learn.

24:9.sourceText: συνεπέθεντο δὲ καὶ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι φάσκοντες ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχειν.
24:9.targetText: The Jews concurred, asserting that these charges were true.

groups.note: συνεπέθεντο ("joined in the attack") is rendered concurred.
ταῦτα ("these things") is rendered these charges.
οὕτως ἔχειν ("to be so") is rendered were true.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English introduces the infinitive clause with that.

24:10.sourceText: Ἀπεκρίθη τε ὁ Παῦλος, νεύσαντος αὐτῷ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος λέγειν Ἐκ πολλῶν ἐτῶν ὄντα σε κριτὴν τῷ ἔθνει τούτῳ ἐπιστάμενος εὐθύμως τὰ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ ἀπολογοῦμαι,
24:10.targetText: When the governor motioned for Paul to speak, he began his response: “Knowing that you have been a judge over this nation for many years, I gladly make my defense.

groups.note: Ἀπεκρίθη ("answered") is rendered began his response.
BSB names Paul in the when-clause and renders Παῦλος here as he.
The genitive absolute νεύσαντος ("having motioned") is rendered as a when-clause.
The pronoun αὐτῷ ("to him") is rendered by the name Paul.
τὰ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ ("the things concerning myself") is rendered my.
ἀπολογοῦμαι ("I defend myself") is rendered I make my defense.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective τε untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English introduces the participle clause with that.

24:11.sourceText: δυναμένου σου ἐπιγνῶναι ὅτι οὐ πλείους εἰσίν μοι ἡμέραι δώδεκα ἀφ’ ἧς ἀνέβην προσκυνήσων εἰς Ἱερουσαλήμ,
24:11.targetText: You can verify for yourself that no more than twelve days ago I went up to Jerusalem to worship.

groups.note: ἐπιγνῶναι ("to find out") is rendered verify.
ἀφ’ ἧς ("since the day when") is rendered ago.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB recasts "there are to me no more than twelve days" without a verb, so εἰσίν μοι has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds for yourself; the Greek has no reflexive word here.

24:12.sourceText: καὶ οὔτε ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ εὗρόν με πρός τινα διαλεγόμενον ἢ ἐπίστασιν ποιοῦντα ὄχλου, οὔτε ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς οὔτε κατὰ τὴν πόλιν,
24:12.targetText: Yet my accusers did not find me debating with anyone in the temple or riling up a crowd in the synagogues or in the city.

groups.note: The καί that links this to verse 11 is rendered Yet.
The first οὔτε ("neither") is rendered not.
ἐπίστασιν ποιοῦντα ("causing a disturbance") is rendered riling up.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB's single not covers the whole list, so this οὔτε ("nor") has no separate English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject that the Greek verb ending implies.

24:13.sourceText: οὐδὲ παραστῆσαι δύνανταί σοι περὶ ὧν νυνὶ κατηγοροῦσίν μου.
24:13.targetText: Nor can they prove to you any of their charges against me.

groups.note: περὶ ὧν ("concerning the things of which") is rendered any of.
κατηγοροῦσιν ("they accuse") is rendered their charges against.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves νυνί ("now") untranslated.

24:14.sourceText: ὁμολογῶ δὲ τοῦτό σοι, ὅτι κατὰ τὴν Ὁδὸν ἣν λέγουσιν αἵρεσιν οὕτως λατρεύω τῷ πατρῴῳ Θεῷ, πιστεύων πᾶσι τοῖς κατὰ τὸν νόμον καὶ τοῖς ἐν τοῖς προφήταις γεγραμμένοις,
24:14.targetText: I do confess to you, however, that I worship the God of our fathers according to the Way, which they call a sect. I believe everything that is laid down by the Law and written in the Prophets,

groups.note: πατρῴῳ ("ancestral") is rendered of our fathers.
The participle πιστεύων ("believing") is rendered I believe, starting a new sentence.
The article τοῖς ("the things") is rendered that.
κατὰ τὸν νόμον ("according to the Law") is rendered laid down by the Law.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves τοῦτο ("this") untranslated.
BSB leaves οὕτως ("so") untranslated.
BSB lets that serve both phrases, so this second τοῖς has no separate English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb of the relative clause.

24:15.sourceText: ἐλπίδα ἔχων εἰς τὸν Θεόν, ἣν καὶ αὐτοὶ οὗτοι προσδέχονται, ἀνάστασιν μέλλειν ἔσεσθαι δικαίων τε καὶ ἀδίκων.
24:15.targetText: and I have the same hope in God that they themselves cherish, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.

groups.note: καί ("also") is rendered by the same: the hope they also hold.
The intensive αὐτοί is rendered themselves.
οὗτοι ("these men") is rendered they.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins ἔχων, rendered I have, to I believe; the Greek has no conjunction here.
English introduces the infinitive clause with that and adds there.

24:16.sourceText: ἐν τούτῳ καὶ αὐτὸς ἀσκῶ ἀπρόσκοπον συνείδησιν ἔχειν πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν καὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους διὰ παντός.
24:16.targetText: In this hope, I strive always to maintain a clear conscience before God and man.

groups.note: τούτῳ ("this") is rendered this hope, pointing back to the hope of verse 15.
διὰ παντός ("through all") is rendered always.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

24:17.sourceText: δι’ ἐτῶν δὲ πλειόνων ἐλεημοσύνας ποιήσων εἰς τὸ ἔθνος μου παρεγενόμην καὶ προσφοράς,
24:17.targetText: After several years, then, I returned to Jerusalem to bring alms to my people and to present offerings.

groups.note: ποιήσων ("to make") governs both alms and offerings; BSB renders it bring and present.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds the destination; the Greek has no word for Jerusalem here.

24:18.sourceText: ἐν αἷς εὗρόν με ἡγνισμένον ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, οὐ μετὰ ὄχλου οὐδὲ μετὰ θορύβου,
24:18.targetText: At the time they found me in the temple, I was ceremonially clean and was not inciting a crowd or an uproar. But there are some Jews from the province of Asia

groups.note: The relative αἷς ("which") is rendered the time.
The participle ἡγνισμένον ("purified") is rendered I was ceremonially clean.
τινὲς δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἀσίας Ἰουδαῖοι, printed at the start of 24:19 in N1904, is rendered in this verse.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB recasts οὐ μετὰ ὄχλου οὐδὲ μετὰ θορύβου ("not with a crowd nor with an uproar") with the verb inciting, so μετά ("with") has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds and was to make a clause; the Greek phrase has no verb or conjunction.
English supplies the verb inciting; the Greek has only μετά ("with") before a crowd and an uproar.
English supplies an existential frame; the Greek has no verb here.
BSB adds that Asia was a Roman province.

24:19.sourceText: τινὲς δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἀσίας Ἰουδαῖοι, οὓς ἔδει ἐπὶ σοῦ παρεῖναι καὶ κατηγορεῖν εἴ τι ἔχοιεν πρὸς ἐμέ.
24:19.targetText: who ought to appear before you and bring charges, if they have anything against me.

sourceMoved.reason: N1904 prints τινὲς δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἀσίας Ἰουδαῖοι at the start of 24:19; BSB renders it at the end of 24:18.

24:20.sourceText: ἢ αὐτοὶ οὗτοι εἰπάτωσαν τί εὗρον ἀδίκημα στάντος μου ἐπὶ τοῦ συνεδρίου,
24:20.targetText: Otherwise, let these men state for themselves any crime they found in me when I stood before the Sanhedrin,

groups.note: ἤ ("or") is rendered Otherwise.
The intensive αὐτοί ("themselves") is rendered for themselves.
The genitive absolute στάντος ("having stood") is rendered as a when-clause.
μου, the subject of the genitive absolute, is rendered I.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds where the crime was found; the Greek has no word for it.

24:21.sourceText: ἢ περὶ μιᾶς ταύτης φωνῆς ἧς ἐκέκραξα ἐν αὐτοῖς ἑστὼς ὅτι Περὶ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν ἐγὼ κρίνομαι σήμερον ἐφ’ ὑμῶν.
24:21.targetText: unless it was this one thing I called out as I stood in their presence: ‘It is concerning the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial before you today.’”

groups.note: ἤ ("than"), continuing the question of verse 20, is rendered unless.
φωνῆς ("utterance") is rendered thing.
αὐτοῖς ("them") is rendered their presence after in.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB recasts "concerning this one utterance" as this one thing, so περί has no English word.
English leaves the relative ἧς ("which") unexpressed.
ὅτι introduces direct speech and is represented by the quotation marks.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and verb for the unless-clause.
English frames the statement as It is … that.
English frames the statement as It is … that.

24:22.sourceText: Ἀνεβάλετο δὲ αὐτοὺς ὁ Φῆλιξ, ἀκριβέστερον εἰδὼς τὰ περὶ τῆς Ὁδοῦ, εἴπας Ὅταν Λυσίας ὁ χιλίαρχος καταβῇ, διαγνώσομαι τὰ καθ’ ὑμᾶς·
24:22.targetText: Then Felix, who was well informed about the Way, adjourned the hearing and said, “When Lysias the commander comes, I will decide your case.”

groups.note: ἀνεβάλετο αὐτούς ("he put them off"), a legal term, is rendered adjourned the hearing.
ἀκριβέστερον ("more accurately") is rendered well.
The participle εἰδώς ("knowing") is rendered who was … informed.
τὰ καθ’ ὑμᾶς ("the matters concerning you") is rendered your case.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves τά ("the things") unexpressed before about the Way.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins said, rendering the participle εἴπας, to the main verb adjourned.

24:23.sourceText: διαταξάμενος τῷ ἑκατοντάρχῃ τηρεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ἔχειν τε ἄνεσιν καὶ μηδένα κωλύειν τῶν ἰδίων αὐτοῦ ὑπηρετεῖν αὐτῷ.
24:23.targetText: He ordered the centurion to keep Paul under guard, but to allow him some freedom and permit his friends to minister to his needs.

groups.note: The participle διαταξάμενος ("having ordered") is rendered He ordered.
The passive τηρεῖσθαι ("to be kept") is rendered keep … under guard.
αὐτόν, the subject of both infinitives, is rendered Paul and then him.
ἔχειν ("to have") is rendered allow him … some freedom.
μηδένα κωλύειν ("to forbid no one") is rendered permit.
τῶν ἰδίων ("his own people") is rendered his friends.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies needs as the object of minister to.

24:24.sourceText: Μετὰ δὲ ἡμέρας τινὰς παραγενόμενος ὁ Φῆλιξ σὺν Δρουσίλλῃ τῇ ἰδίᾳ γυναικὶ οὔσῃ Ἰουδαίᾳ μετεπέμψατο τὸν Παῦλον, καὶ ἤκουσεν αὐτοῦ περὶ τῆς εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν πίστεως.
24:24.targetText: After several days, Felix returned with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jewess. He sent for Paul and listened to him speak about faith in Christ Jesus.

groups.note: The participle παραγενόμενος ("having arrived") is rendered returned.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb for what Paul said; the Greek has only ἤκουσεν αὐτοῦ ("heard him").

24:25.sourceText: διαλεγομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ περὶ δικαιοσύνης καὶ ἐγκρατείας καὶ τοῦ κρίματος τοῦ μέλλοντος ἔμφοβος γενόμενος ὁ Φῆλιξ ἀπεκρίθη Τὸ νῦν ἔχον πορεύου, καιρὸν δὲ μεταλαβὼν μετακαλέσομαί σε·
24:25.targetText: As Paul expounded on righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment, Felix became frightened and said, “You may go for now. When I find the time, I will call for you.”

groups.note: The genitive absolute διαλεγομένου ("while he was discussing") is rendered as an as-clause.
The pronoun αὐτοῦ ("he") is rendered by the name Paul.
τοῦ μέλλοντος ("the one to come") is rendered coming.
ἀπεκρίθη ("answered") is rendered said.
τὸ νῦν ἔχον ("as for now") is rendered for now.
The participle μεταλαβών ("having found") is rendered as a when-clause.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
BSB lists the three topics with a comma, so this καί has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins became frightened, rendering the participle γενόμενος, to the main verb said.

24:26.sourceText: ἅμα καὶ ἐλπίζων ὅτι χρήματα δοθήσεται αὐτῷ ὑπὸ τοῦ Παύλου· διὸ καὶ πυκνότερον αὐτὸν μεταπεμπόμενος ὡμίλει αὐτῷ.
24:26.targetText: At the same time, he was hoping that Paul would offer him a bribe. So he sent for Paul frequently and talked with him.

groups.note: The participle ἐλπίζων ("hoping") is rendered he was hoping.
χρήματα ("money") is rendered a bribe.
The passive δοθήσεται ("would be given") is rendered as an active, would offer.
The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered by the name Paul.
The participle μεταπεμπόμενος ("sending for") is rendered he sent for.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.
BSB turns the passive into an active, so ὑπό ("by") has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins sent for, rendering the participle μεταπεμπόμενος, to the main verb talked.

24:27.sourceText: Διετίας δὲ πληρωθείσης ἔλαβεν διάδοχον ὁ Φῆλιξ Πόρκιον Φῆστον· θέλων τε χάριτα καταθέσθαι τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὁ Φῆλιξ κατέλιπε τὸν Παῦλον δεδεμένον.
24:27.targetText: After two years had passed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus. And wishing to do the Jews a favor, Felix left Paul in prison.

groups.note: The genitive absolute πληρωθείσης ("having been completed") is rendered as an after-clause.
ἔλαβεν διάδοχον ("received a successor") is rendered was succeeded by.
δεδεμένον ("bound") is rendered in prison.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
